chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raising it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man dies in the ship and it is not possible to reach the coast, he is enshrouded, embalmed, wrapped in a cloth, and cast into the water.

key_terms.يُكَفَّنُ: He is enshrouded (wrapped in burial cloths)

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for burying someone who dies on a ship far from the coast?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the principle of *ease* (taysir) in Shia jurisprudence, adapting the standard land-based burial rites for the unique constraints of maritime death. It specifies that while the body is washed, shrouded, and perfumed as usual, the final interment occurs directly in the water, reflecting the practical necessity when reaching the shore is impossible. This precedent is often cited by jurists to justify variations in burial rituals based on environmental feasibility.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, 
(It has been narrated) raising it from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the man dies in the ship and it is not able upon (getting to the) coast, he should be enshrouded, and embalmed, and wrapped in a cloth, and would be cast into the sea’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad in a marfu‘ manner has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one dies in a ship and it is not possible to bring him to the shore, shroud and hunut are done for him, after wrapping in a piece of cloth, is thrown into the water.’”
